title: fix(discord): avoid unused Activity transport work during discovery
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Discord capability discovery initializing the optional Activity message sender even when no widget is requested or Activities is disabled.

## User Impact

Discord discovery does less unused startup work. Widget routing, persistence, delivery receipts, and rollback behavior remain unchanged. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Import the sender inside the existing asynchronous presentation operation and its error/rollback boundary. A configured Discord provider also loads this graph through interactive handlers before provider readiness, so this does not eliminate all Discord startup cost or independently resolve Gateway plugin stalls.

The production change replaces one import and adds one dynamic import. The existing registration cases now protect the unused transport initialization boundary; the Linux benchmark records actual external plugin selection and process costs.

## Evidence

- Registration cases fail on the base with one eager sender initialization and pass with zero. Nine registration/presenter tests pass, including delivery and rollback bookkeeping.
- Full build, targeted types/lint/format, and fresh independent P0-P2 review pass.
- The maintained isolated Gateway/Crabline case passes on Bun and explicitly on Node: channel ready, agent/model inventory, first public widget launch-button receipt, mismatched routes hidden, inline widget fallback, and completed cleanup. Node startup was 18.625 seconds and the selected semantic case took 8.263 seconds; that case duration is not an isolated first-send timing.
- Clean-head cold-import memory qualification passes on `9fdfbc8c0817` with matching source/build identity and verified child cleanup: 111.781 MiB peak RSS / 221.234 ms CPU delta.

Five interleaved cold-process pairs on Linux/Node 26.12.1, with fresh isolated state, compile cache and network disabled, and warm filesystem cache:

| Metric | Baseline median / p95 | Lazy sender median / p95 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Full native CLI inspection | 40.418 / 41.556 s | 37.600 / 38.200 s |
| Discord registration | 27.832 / 28.426 s | 25.437 / 25.874 s |
| Process CPU | 23.02 / 23.11 s | 21.40 / 21.90 s |
| Peak RSS | 644928 / 651140 KiB | 601876 / 635328 KiB |

The lazy change alone does not meet the original 20% acceptance threshold. Combined qualification with the worker wakeup repair in #180973 meets the original rule, as recorded below; the combined gain is not attributed solely to this Discord change.

<details>
<summary>Combined packaged Linux acceptance declared before measurement</summary>

Use committed `scripts/bench-plugin-registration.mts` with baseline and candidate host entrypoints and exact external plugin roots, five serial interleaved pairs, fresh isolated HOME/state/workspace, supported identical Node, no credentials or network, and host load recorded. Both discovery-load and registration medians must improve by at least 20%, with each p95 no worse than baseline and all ten selected plugin loads exiting zero with status loaded. Record full elapsed/CPU/RSS medians, p95, and spread; investigate regressions under the normal performance policy.

Command: `node scripts/bench-plugin-registration.mts BASELINE_ENTRY CANDIDATE_ENTRY discord BASELINE_PLUGIN_ROOT CANDIDATE_PLUGIN_ROOT 5` inside an isolated Linux network namespace. The script requires GNU time and timeout. Frozen artifact identities and the resulting table are recorded below.

</details>

Packaged Linux combined qualification (five interleaved pairs; cold processes/state, warm filesystem cache):

| Metric | Baseline median / p95 | IPC + lazy sender median / p95 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Full CLI inspection | 40.903 / 42.119 s | 19.379 / 20.339 s |
| Profiled discovery load | 71.8 / 102.8 ms | 44.5 / 85.8 ms |
| Registration | 28.053 / 28.266 s | 6.225 / 7.513 s |
| Process CPU | 23.360 / 24.040 s | 20.740 / 20.850 s |
| Peak RSS | 643,968 / 648,624 KiB | 632,872 / 641,652 KiB |

Both original phase-median improvement thresholds and p95 limits pass; all ten native inspections exited zero with exactly one loaded Discord plugin at its requested external root. Other reported medians and p95 values improve. The one-minute host load spans 0.24–3.98 across the cohort and is recorded per sample. Five observations per arm make the reported empirical p95 the largest observed sample.

The baseline is official core `bd8424ab76db61bda5b2c8cd1e76041a7704e848` (archive SHA256 `1cbb250b3b649a1e9a868f52a326d2deddc7e976195506533e1dc59cb3e79ab4`); candidate core is `cabd7931f131c26f9570d2738a9d988f3f3162af` (archive SHA256 `b688358fe1c9af736d0fb14937bf9519397b16e3d4f734fd2f32d2fa61fb6ebe`). External baseline/fixed Discord archives have SHA256 `b4fc18b269d3eef2676bea89b668be66c7d29e37f678d767f27394c0a147db02` / `bf5c0abcd2fed28e67fcf3bdbdf364c9bd746a77fea135b99aa4de207897ce5b`. The fixed plugin archive retains its original reviewed dirty-build provenance; its runtime source matches the committed fix. This is a benchmark candidate, not an official production release.

The workload is commit `3996752201d228a717b49900b3c8c5046c763726`, SHA256 `f00a2b71e0200578c835fa25b81483efecb7ad514da6348ec0f541d617f517f0`; identical Linux Node26.12.1 binaries have SHA256 `08f12d42fb304468e8ee86247fe686aae5b225836ea65e9d6566c11ae6ba2e8e`. Post-run complete external plugin/dependency tree snapshots are byte-identical to the frozen pre-run snapshots (6,452 baseline / 6,456 candidate entries). A separate instrumented diagnostic records 9,591 Atomics waits totaling 2.125 seconds, compared with the earlier stock diagnostic's 10,480 waits / 22.320 seconds; its instrumented wall time is excluded from the ABAB cohort. Native SDK coverage resolves only from the candidate core prefix. Full packaged Gateway qualification remains a deployment preflight. The combined table does not attribute the whole gain to the Discord-only change.
